To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

– (i) quantum circuit simulation is possible with the use of HDLs, (ii) bubble bit technique is effective for improving quantum circuit simulation speed, (iii) fault injection is possible in the quantum circuit framework, (iv) fault tolerant stabilizer quantum computation is benefic in terms of reliability, (v) reliability assessment methodologies from Embryonics are applicable to quantum computation and (vi) accuracy threshold is the appropriate reliability measure for Embryonic memories.

we have developed an efficient simulation framework, based on HDL, for the quantum circuit model, we have developed a technique for avoiding entangled representation of states in quantum circuits, we have shown that the reliability of reconfigurable quantum gates can be assessed by the accuracy threshold and that the reliability of stabilizer encoded quantum computation can be assessed by a modified accuracy threshold.

we developed an efficient quantum circuit simulator that is able to handle large scale problems, and that we found common ground for reliability assessment methodologies between the Embryoncis project and quantum computation.
